title: English Podcast for Learning English | Real English Conversation | CHANGE YOUR LIFE BEFORE 2027

sentences.t: Hello and welcome back to Leo English podcast.
We're very happy you're here with us today.
I'm Tina.
And I'm Leo.
This channel helps you learn English through real conversation, useful vocabulary, and simple daily practice.
We want English to feel natural, clear, and possible for you.
And today's topic is big, exciting, and very useful.
We're talking about how to change your life before 2027.
Yes, this topic matters because many people want a better life, but they don't know where to begin.
Today, we show you simple English, and simple ideas you can use in real life.
We're going to talk about habits, goals, daily routines, mistakes, and small changes that can make a big difference.
And while we talk, you'll learn English for self-improvement, daily life, motivation, and real conversation.
So, if you want better English, and maybe a better life, too.
Stay with us.
If you enjoy learning with us, please like this video and subscribe to the channel
and click the bell, too, so you don't miss our next lesson.
All right, let's get started.
How are you today, Leo?
I'm pretty good.
I'm a little tired, but in a hopeful way.
In a hopeful way.
Yes. I wake up late, but I still believe in myself.
That is a very generous attitude.
Thank you. How are you today?
I'm good. I feel focused today.
I make my tea at 7:10.
I check my notes at 7:20.
And I start work at 8.
You always sound like a person who wins mornings.
I don't always win.
Sometimes I also look at my phone too long.
Really? Oh, I do that too.
Yesterday I check one message and then suddenly 20 minutes disappear.
That happens to many people.
What do you do this weekend?
On Saturday, I clean my room for 40 minutes.
Then I find an old notebook with goals from 2 years ago.
That sounds interesting.
What kinds of goals?
Some are good.
One says read more.
One says sleep earlier.
One says become a different person by Tuesday.
By Tuesday.
Yes. Past Leo is very ambitious and very unrealistic.
That is a great example.
Actually, many people want a big life change very fast.
Exactly. They want a new body, new job, new routine, and perfect skin by next week.
And then they feel disappointed when real life moves more slowly.
Speaking of changing too much too fast, that sounds like our topic today.
It does. Today we're talking about how to change your life before 2027 in a realistic way.
Good, because I want a better life, but I also want a plan that normal humans can follow.
Then this conversation is for you.
Okay, Leo, let's start with the biggest question.
What does change your life before 2027 really mean?
For me, it doesn't mean becoming a completely new person.
It means improving the life I already have.
I agree. That is a very healthy way to see it.
Real change usually means better habits, clearer priorities, and more honest daily choices.
Wait, what does priorities mean?
Priorities are the things that matter most.
They are the things you choose to give time, energy, and attention to.
So, if sleep is my priority, I don't watch cooking videos at 1:00 a.m.
Exactly. Your actions should match your priorities.
That sounds simple but also painful.
Sometimes the truth is painful.
So where should people begin if they want change before 2027?
I think they should begin with one honest question.
What is not working in my life right now?
That's interesting. Not what looks cool online, but what is actually not working?
Exactly. Maybe you feel tired every day.
Maybe your money disappears too quickly.
Maybe your room is always messy.
Maybe you say you want English, but you never practice.
Ouch, that last one hits hard.
It hits many people.
I think people also try to fix 10 things at once.
Yes. And that usually fails.
Research on habit change often shows that small and consistent action works better than extreme action.
Can you give an example?
Sure. If someone sleeps at 1:30 every night, a realistic goal is not tomorrow I sleep at 9.
A better goal is this week I sleep at 12:45.
That sounds less dramatic but more possible.
Exactly. Real change should feel possible.
I have a question.
What is the difference between a goal and a system?
Good question. A goal is the result you want.
A system is the repeated action that helps you get there.
So, I want better English as a goal,
right? And I listen and speak English for 15 minutes every day is a system.
Oh, I like that.
The goal sounds exciting, but the system does the real work.
Exactly. Systems build results over time.
Then maybe the first life change before 2027 is to stop loving goals and start respecting systems.
Very nicely said.
Thank you. I surprise myself sometimes.
Let's break this topic into main life areas.
I think five areas matter a lot.
Health, time, money, relationships, and learning.
Good. That feels organized.
My brain thanks you.
Let's start with health.
If your body feels bad, everything feels harder.
Really? Even emails?
Yes, even emails.
If you sleep badly, eat badly, and never move, your focus gets weaker.
I noticed that when I sleep 6 hours for three nights, everything feels louder and harder.
Exactly. So, simple health changes matter.
Sleep 30 minutes earlier.
Walk 20 minutes a day.
Drink more water.
Eat one better meal.
I like simple health advice.
Sometimes online advice sounds like military training.
Yes. And extreme plans often do not last.
I start walking after dinner three times a week last month.
That's great. How long do you walk?
About 25 minutes.
Sometimes 30 if I'm thinking about life for snacks.
That is a perfect example.
Small habits can improve more than one part of life.
So, health change doesn't always mean a gym membership and six protein drinks.
No. For many people, it starts with sleep, water, walking, and regular meals.
Okay. What about time?
Time is a big one.
Many people say, "I don't have time."
But often the deeper truth is, I don't use my time clearly.
Oof, another painful truth.
I know, but it helps.
Try this. For 3 days, write down how you spend your time.
Like a time log.
Exactly. A time log is a simple record of how you use your hours.
So, what does record mean here?
It means you write it down so you can check it later.
Got it. So, if I say I have no time, but I watch videos for 2 hours, the notebook will tell the truth.
Yes, the notebook is honest.
Rude, but honest.
Very rude sometimes.
I do this once and I notice something embarrassing.
I waste 15 minutes here, 10 minutes there, 20 minutes somewhere else.
By night, I lose more than 1 hour.
That is very common.
Time often disappears in small pieces.
So, what is a good fix?
Choose one anchor habit.
For example, every weekday at 8:30 p.m.
you do one important thing for 20 minutes.
Why call it an anchor habit?
Because it gives structure to your day.
It holds something in place.
Like an anchor holds a boat.
Ah, nice image.
So my life boat stops floating everywhere.
What kind of important thing?
It depends on your life.
English practice, job search, budgeting, reading, stretching, planning tomorrow, or cleaning one small area.
I like that.
Not a huge change, just one strong action in one fixed place.
Yes, simple and repeatable.
Okay, next area.
Money. People get nervous when money appears in the conversation.
That's true. But money habits shape life very strongly.
You do not need to be rich to improve your money life.
You need awareness.
What does awareness mean?
Awareness means you notice what is happening clearly.
So with money, awareness means I know where it goes.
Exactly. Many people want more savings, but they never check their spending carefully.
I do that too.
I buy coffee, snacks, one random notebook, then another snack, and later I act surprised.
Small spending is not always bad.
The problem is unconscious spending.
That's interesting. So, one life change before 2027 could be, I check my money every week.
Yes. A weekly money check can change a lot.
Look at what comes in, what goes out, and what repeats.
Repeats like subscriptions.
Yes. Subscriptions, delivery fees, impulse shopping, daily drinks, and little habits that quietly grow.
I once pay for a language app for 4 months and forget about it.
That happens more than people think.
So, money improvement is not always make more.
Sometimes it is leak less.
Very well said.
Spend with intention, not only with emotion.
What about relationships?
That sounds more emotional.
It is emotional, but very important.
Before 2027, many people need to change who they spend time with, how they speak, and what boundaries they keep.
Wait, what does boundaries mean?
Boundaries are limits.
They show what is okay for you and what is not okay.
So if someone calls me every night at 11:45 to complain, I can say, "I care about you, but I need rest."
Yes, that is a healthy boundary.
Good, because night Leo is not wise.
Many people feel tired because they say yes too often.
They give time they do not have.
They listen when they need rest.
They stay close to people who drain them.
Dream means take energy away, right?
I learned this slowly.
I used to think being kind meant always being available.
That is a very common mistake.
Real kindness can include honesty and limits.
So, changing your life before 2027 may also mean protecting your peace.
Absolutely. Better relationships and better boundaries can improve your whole week.
I notice that when I spend 2 hours with positive people, I feel lighter.
But when I spend 20 minutes with the wrong person, I feel tired for the rest of the day.
That is a very real experience.
Okay, let's talk about learning.
This one matters a lot for our viewers.
Yes, many people want to learn English, new work skills, or something that improves their future, but they wait for motivation.
Motivation is so dramatic.
It arrives like a movie star and leaves after one rainy day.
That is true.
Motivation can help.
But routine is more dependable.
Dependable means something I can trust.
Exactly. Something reliable and steady.
So if I want better English before 2027, I should not ask, do I feel inspired today?
I should ask what is today's small practice?
Perfect. That's the right mindset.
I think people also make practice too big.
They say I will study for 2 hours every day and then they disappear.
Yes, a small daily practice is stronger than a huge plan you can't keep.
What is a good English routine
for beginners or lower intermediate learners?
I suggest this.
10 minutes of listening, five minutes of speaking out loud, and five minutes of review.
That's 20 minutes total.
That sounds realistic.
Yes. Do it 5 days a week.
After 3 months, you'll feel a difference.
Yes. Improvement may feel slow day by day, but over months, it becomes clear.
I think people quit because they expect to feel different in 4 days.
Exactly. Real change is often quiet at first.
Quiet change. I like that phrase.
Me too.
Can we talk about one more thing?
Yes, that is very important.
Sometimes people say, "I want to change my life."
But deep inside they still believe I'm lazy.
I always fail or I'm not the kind of person who changes.
That is a powerful point.
If your identity stays negative, your habits struggle to grow.
So instead of saying, "I'm terrible at routines," I can say, "I'm learning to become more consistent."
Exactly. That sentence opens the door.
It gives you movement.
Consistent means doing something regularly, right?
Yes. Not perfectly, regularly.
That word helps me.
I don't need to become a superhero.
I need to become more consistent.
Exactly. And before 2027, consistency can change a great deal.
Can we make a simple action plan for viewers?
Yes. Let's make a five-step plan.
Great. People love steps.
My brain especially loves steps.
Step one, choose one life area that needs attention most right now.
Health, time, money, relationships, or learning.
Step two, write one honest sentence about the problem
like I sleep too late or I waste money on small things.
Exactly. Step three, choose one tiny daily or weekly action
like I sleep 30 minutes earlier or I check my spending every Sunday.
Perfect. Step four, put the action in a real time and place.
For example, at 900 p.m.
after dinner, I study English for 20 minutes.
Perfect. Step five, track it for two weeks and notice what changes.
What does track it mean?
It means you keep a simple record.
Maybe on paper, maybe on your phone.
So, if I do it, I mark it.
Yes. Seeing progress helps motivation stay stronger.
I think another helpful idea is to make life easier for your future self.
That is excellent advice.
For example, putting your book on the table, filling your water bottle early, or choosing clothes the night before.
Yes. Good habits grow better when the environment supports them.
Environment means the space around you and the things in it.
Exactly. Your room, your desk, your phone, your kitchen, your schedule.
These things affect behavior.
That makes so much sense.
If my phone is next to my pillow, I scroll.
If it is across the room, I sleep more.
Exactly. Good systems reduce unnecessary struggle.
So before 2027, maybe the real goal is not become perfect.
Maybe it is build a life that helps me do better things more often.
I think that is beautifully said.
Thank you. I become wise after minute 40.
Then we should keep recording.
Please do.
Let's end the main conversation with one message.
You do not need a dramatic new life by tomorrow.
You need honest change, small action, and steady repetition.
Yes, one better habit, one clearer choice, one stronger routine.
That is enough to begin.
And if you begin now, you can look very different by 2027.
Not like a movie character, like a real person with a calmer, stronger life.
Exactly. You know, Leo, while we were talking, we used many useful words and phrases.
Let's study them together.
Yes, please. My brain likes a good clean list.
First word, priority.
This means the thing that matters most.
Oh yes, I need this word in my life.
Exactly. For example, sleep is a priority for me this month.
Another example is my top priority is daily English practice.
And you can also say family is my priority right now.
A usage tip is to say a priority for one important thing or priorities for several.
What's your biggest priority this week?
My biggest priority is getting enough sleep because I feel better when I rest well.
Next word, realistic.
This means possible and sensible in real life.
Oh, yes. This word saves people from silly plans.
Exactly. For example, a realistic goal is 20 minutes of study a day.
Another example is it is not realistic for me to wake up at 4:30 tomorrow.
And you can also say I need a realistic schedule, not a fantasy schedule.
The opposite is unrealistic.
What is one realistic change for you?
One realistic change for me is walking after dinner three times a week.
Next word, system.
This means a repeated way of doing something.
Oh yes, the system does the real work.
Exactly. For example, my system is simple.
Study after breakfast every day.
Another example is a good system makes habits easier.
And you can also say, I trust my system more than my mood.
That is a great sentence.
What system helps you most?
My notes system helps me remember tasks because I forget things very easily.
Next phrase, time log.
This means a record of how you spend your time.
Oh yes, the honest notebook.
Exactly. For example, I keep a time log for 3 days.
Another example is my time log shows I waste 40 minutes in the morning.
And you can also say a time log helps me see my real habits.
A related word is schedule, but a time log records what already happened.
What does your time log usually show?
It usually shows that my phone steals more time than I think.
Next word, awareness.
This means clear understanding of what is happening.
Oh yes, especially with money and habits.
Exactly. For example, awareness helps people change their spending.
Another example is I want more awareness about how I use my evenings.
And you can also say awareness is the first step to change.
That is a strong sentence.
What do you want more awareness about?
I want more awareness about what makes me tired at the end of the day.
Next word, boundary.
This means a healthy limit.
Oh, yes. This word is very useful and sometimes very difficult.
Exactly. For example, I set a boundary and stop replying after 10 p.m.
Another example is a boundary protects my peace.
And you can also say, it is okay to have boundaries with people you care about.
Very true. A common mistake is thinking boundaries are rude.
They are not rude when they are clear and respectful.
What boundary helps you most?
My best boundary is not checking messages late at night.
Next word, consistent.
This means regular and steady over time.
Oh yes, not perfect, just regular.
Exactly. For example, she is consistent with her morning walk.
Another example is small consistent effort brings real results.
And you can also say I want to become more consistent with my English practice.
A usage tip is we often say consistent with a habit or activity.
What do you want to become more consistent with?
I want to become more consistent with sleep because it changes everything for me.
Next word, track.
This means record and check progress over time.
Oh yes, I like this word because it feels practical.
Exactly. For example, I track my habits in a small notebook.
Another example is we track spending every Sunday.
And you can also say tracking helps me stay honest.
Very nice. What do you track now if anything?
I track my walks because checking the boxes makes me happy.
Next word, environment.
This means the space and conditions around you.
Oh, yes. The room, the desk, the phone, the snacks, all of it.
Exactly. For example, my environment affects my focus.
Another example is a clean desk creates a better work environment.
And you can also say I change my environment to support better habits.
Good. A tip is to make good actions easier and bad actions harder.
What part of your environment helps you most?
My desk helps me most when it's clean and simple.
Next phrase, quiet change.
This means improvement that happens slowly and calmly.
Oh yes, I really like this phrase.
Exactly. For example, better sleep creates quiet change over time.
Another example is daily practice brings quiet change to your English.
And you can also say I don't need dramatic change.
Quiet change is enough.
That is a beautiful sentence.
What quiet change do you want most?
I want quiet change in my routine because I want calmer days.
Great. Now let's do a quick summary list.
Yes. List time.
Priority. The thing that matters most.
Realistic. possible and sensible in real life.
System, a repeated way of doing something.
Time log, a record of how you spend your time.
Awareness, clear understanding of what is happening.
Boundary, a healthy limit.
Consistent, regular and steady over time.
Track, record, and check progress.
Environment, the space and conditions around you.
Quiet change. Slow, calm improvement over time.
Okay, Leo, that was a lot of talking about changing your life before 2027.
Yes, it was.
I feel like my brain just went to a very helpful meeting.
Let's think about what we learned.
First, we learned that life change does not mean becoming a totally different person overnight.
We use phrases like small steps, realistic change, and honest action.
Then we talked about goals and systems.
A goal is what you want, but a system is what you do regularly.
After that, we looked at important life areas.
We talked about health, time, money, relationships, and learning.
We used phrases like sleep earlier, keep a time log, check your spending, and set boundaries.
Then we talked about consistency.
We said small action repeated many times is stronger than one big dramatic plan.
Yes. And we learned that better matters more than perfect.
After that we discussed identity and mindset.
We said it helps to think I am learning to become more consistent instead of using negative labels.
That part is really important.
The way you talk to yourself changes the way you act.
Finally, we made a simple five-step action plan.
Choose one life area, write the real problem, pick one small action, give it a time and place, and track it.
So, the big message is simple.
If you want change before 2027, start now, start small, and stay steady.
Exactly. You do not need a perfect life this week.
You need one useful step today
and then another one tomorrow.
Now we want to hear from you.
This is our favorite part.
Yes, because now you join the conversation.
Our question of the day is, what is one small change you want to make before 2027 and why?
I'll answer first.
I want to become more consistent with sleep because good sleep improves my mood, focus, and energy.
That is a great answer.
My answer is a little different.
I want to protect my time better because clear time helps every other part of life.
See, we have different answers and that's okay.
So viewers, we want to know about you.
Maybe you want to improve your English.
Maybe you want better money habits.
Maybe you want a calmer routine.
Here are some example answers you can copy.
One small change I want to make before 2027 is this is because
I want to improve my blank by doing blank every day.
My goal is blank and my first small step is blank.
Please tell us in the comments.
Write before 2027 I want to change blank.
I will start by blank
or write one habit I want is blank because it will help me blank.
It helps us make better videos and helps you practice writing.
So, please share your answer.
We really want to read it.
Thank you so much for spending this time with us today.
We're really glad you practice English and life skills with us.
If this lesson helps you, give this video a big thumbs up.
Click the subscribe button and the little bell.
That way you won't forget to join us for our next lesson.
You are all great students and we're proud of your effort.
Keep practicing. Remember, a small habit repeated many times can change your future.
Yes, start simple, stay honest, and keep going.
Have a wonderful day, evening, and night.
Take care of yourself and keep moving forward.
Goodbye. Bye everyone.
